title: S Harrison Smith re-signing with Vikings for 15th season: Source
content:
The Minnesota Vikings are re-signing safety and franchise legend Harrison Smith for the 2026 season, a league source told The Athletic on condition of anonymity because the deal is not yet official. Smith, 37, will return for his 15th season on a one-year, $12.25 million deal with incentives up to $16.25 million.

For months, Smith’s future seemed up in the air. The team celebrated him at U.S. Bank Stadium toward the end of the 2025 season. Still, Smith never officially announced his retirement. Some Vikings staffers and players expected him to ride off into the sunset, or at least to wait until after the first few games before making his decision. Instead, he’ll be back, hoping to build off his exceptional end to last season. The Vikings open the season Sept. 13 against the Green Bay Packers.

Minnesota needed Smith with the current dynamics of its safety room. Offseason signing Jamal Adams tore a quad. In recent weeks, safeties Theo Jackson, Jakobe Thomas and Jacob Thomas all suffered injuries, complicating the secondary configuration for a team that likes to play with three safeties.

Smith not only provides depth but also allows defensive coordinator Brian Flores to position fellow defenders like Josh Metellus in their optimal spots.

Smith finished the 2025 season on a heater. He intercepted two passes and recorded one sack in the final five games. There were spurts of emotion down the stretch, but even he admitted how much better he felt physically.

A personal health matter slowed the beginning of his 2025 campaign. He couldn’t participate in training camp, which hurt his offseason preparations. When he did come back in Week 3, the Vikings didn’t ask him to take on a full workload of snaps. Smith’s playing time ticked up when Minnesota finished its two-week stint in Europe.

By the end of the season, Flores was conferring with Smith on preferences before games. This led to a string of heavy blitz performances.

Flores’ extension likely made Smith’s decision to return easier, as the coach and safety are a nearly perfect match. Smith appreciates Flores’ creativity, and Flores respects Smith’s ability to call the game from the field. Smith’s presence will allow for some continuity on defense amid a roster transformation to navigate the team’s salary-cap deficit.

A first-round pick of the Vikings in 2012 out of Notre Dame, Smith has played in 207 games for the franchise, has been named to six Pro Bowls and is the NFL’s active leader in interceptions with 39.
